:::{#exm-empirical-risk}
#### Empirical risk of a birth-weight model under squared error

The `birthwt` data record the birth weight in grams of babies born at Baystate Medical Center in Springfield, Massachusetts [@hosmer1989applied],
as distributed in R's `MASS` package [@venables2002modern].
We fit a [linear regression](basic-statistical-methods.qmd#def-linear-regression) of birth weight on the mother's weight at her last menstrual period and her smoking status.
We use every third row as the [held-out set](#def-held-out-set) and fit on the remaining rows, the [training set](#def-training-set).
The [loss](#def-observation-loss) is the squared error, so the empirical risk is the mean of the squared prediction errors.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

##### R

```{r}
#| label: empirical-risk-r
#| code-fold: false
birthwt <- read.csv("data/birthwt.csv")
is_held_out <- seq_len(nrow(birthwt)) %% 3 == 0

fit_bwt <- lm(bwt ~ lwt + smoke, data = birthwt[!is_held_out, ])

empirical_risk <- function(data) {
  mean((data$bwt - predict(fit_bwt, newdata = data))^2)
}

empirical_risks <- c(
  training = empirical_risk(birthwt[!is_held_out, ]),
  held_out = empirical_risk(birthwt[is_held_out, ])
)
empirical_risks
```

##### Python

```{python}
#| label: empirical-risk-py
#| code-fold: false
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf

birthwt = pd.read_csv("data/birthwt.csv")
is_held_out = (np.arange(1, len(birthwt) + 1) % 3 == 0)

fit_bwt = smf.ols("bwt ~ lwt + smoke", data=birthwt[~is_held_out]).fit()


def empirical_risk(data):
    return ((data["bwt"] - fit_bwt.predict(data)) ** 2).mean()


empirical_risks = {
    "training": empirical_risk(birthwt[~is_held_out]),
    "held_out": empirical_risk(birthwt[is_held_out]),
}
empirical_risks
```

:::

Of the `r nrow(birthwt)` babies, `r sum(!is_held_out)` are in the [training set](#def-training-set).
The [fitted model](#def-fitted-model) has an [empirical risk](#def-empirical-risk) of
`r format(round(empirical_risks[["training"]]), big.mark = ",")` squared grams on the training set
and `r format(round(empirical_risks[["held_out"]]), big.mark = ",")` squared grams on the held-out set.
Its square root, `r round(sqrt(empirical_risks[["training"]]))` grams, is the typical size of a training prediction error.

:::
